_meta.description: Everything Aperion did: mount and camera control, offline plate solving, auto-align, live stacking, mosaics, the hardware it ran on, and why it was shelved.
a-firmware-patch-solves.cd67be: A firmware patch solves it on the device instead
all-capture-plate-solving.ecf1eb: All capture, plate solving, and stacking happens on your device — no servers, no accounts.
aperion-runs-end-to.1071e8: Aperion runs end-to-end on this stack — and degrades gracefully without it.
aperion-talked-to-the.41ff89: Aperion talked to the Benro Polaris over a reverse-engineered BLE + TCP protocol. That is fine for a personal tool and a hard sell as a shipping product: the control path is undocumented, unsupported, and could break with any mount firmware update, and getting it sanctioned — by Benro, or through App Store review — was never a bet worth building a release around. Since my own Polaris is well past its warranty period, there was also nothing left to protect by staying on the sanctioned side of that line.
aperion-triggers-the-camera.f8cd4b: Aperion triggers the camera over CCAPI and pulls the JPEG preview down the network.
app-store-approval-was.0c8cdb: App Store approval was never a realistic bet
benro-polaris-ble-wake.8378b2: Benro Polaris BLE wake + TCP 9090 rocker protocol
blaine-miller-all-rights.b327c2: © Blaine Miller. All rights reserved.
browse-the-catalog-the.a7ff59: Browse the catalog, the AR sky chart, or visible-tonight filtered by altitude.
canon-eos-with-ccapi.b8d755: Canon EOS with CCAPI — tested on R5 Mark II (firmware 1.2)
everything-below-describes-the.dfc9ea: Everything below describes the app as it was built. It was never released, and none of it is available to download — see why it's shelved.
for-motion-timelapses-set.84cbb0: For motion timelapses, set a start pose and an end pose, pick a duration and frame rate, and let the linear interpolator drive the mount. Toggle sidereal tracking to keep the stars pinned while the landscape rolls beneath them.
frame-your-two-corners.c889ac: Frame your two corners from the joystick. Aperion computes the tile grid, the overlap, and walks the mount through every panel — capturing each frame with the same exposure ladder.
from-tap-to-framed.0faf37: From Tap to Framed in Seconds
full-mount-joystick-camera.19f906: Full mount joystick, camera-setting wheels, plate-solve trigger, and a zoomable preview — right on your wrist. Works over Bluetooth even when your phone is on the mount's hotspot.
ios-26-a15-or.c99a97: iOS 26, A15 or newer (ARKit orientation tracking)
it-was-planned-as.9c2e53: It was planned as a $9.99 universal purchase. It never shipped, and it isn't going to.
libgphoto2-nikon-sony-fuji.bf09d4: libgphoto2 Nikon, Sony, Fuji, Olympus over USB tether — anything gphoto2 supports
linear-pan-between-start.2b2433: Linear pan between start and end poses at your chosen frame rate. Optional sidereal tracking pins the stars while the foreground drifts.
most-plate-solving-workflows.6d9dc2: Most plate-solving workflows assume you have a reliable internet connection at your dark site. You don't. Aperion ships the catalog and the pattern matcher inside the app and runs the solve on the device's neural and CPU cores.
mount-control-relied-on.3d8d76: Mount control relied on an unofficial protocol
my-polaris-is-out.c166b5: My Polaris is out of warranty — nothing to risk
neither-benro-nor-apple.cacbe4: Neither Benro nor Apple had reason to bless it
no-mount-a-plain.e6a792: No mount? A plain tripod works too. The slew and goto controls politely grey themselves out; capture, offline plate solving, live stacks, and the AR sky chart all still run as expected.
no-swapping-between-the.74ddb8: No swapping between the Polaris app, Canon's control utility, and a plate-solving service. Aperion unified the entire capture loop.
one-screen-drives-the.4247e6: One screen drives the Benro Polaris mount over BLE + TCP and a Canon EOS body over CCAPI. Joystick, shutter, ISO wheels, and target picker all live together.
pairing-happens-automatically-over.76150: Pairing happens automatically over WatchConnectivity even when the phone is joined to the mount's offline Wi-Fi network — a surprisingly hard problem that Aperion just handles.
patching-the-mount-s.2c4290: Patching the mount's firmware directly turned out to be the better workaround. The intelligence lives on the device rather than in a phone app, so the Polaris runs a full session — slews, dwells, shutter triggers — without my phone tethered to it and without an app driving it all night. No dead battery, no dropped BLE link at 3 a.m., no session lost because a phone locked up.
plate-solving-that-actually.a151d0: Plate Solving That Actually Works in the Field
point-your-phone-at.17f719: Point your phone at the sky and see labeled targets overlaid via ARKit. Tap a galaxy or nebula to slew the mount and start the capture.
same-source-tree-same.3f940e: Same source tree, same controls, larger workspace. Review the night's gallery, reprocess RAW frames, and rebuild stacks at desktop scale.
set-two-corners-from.0b250e: Set two corners from the joystick and Aperion walks the rectangular grid for you with configurable overlap. Capture wide-field panels of the Milky Way without doing the trig.
shoot-solve-sync-nudge.46023a: Shoot → solve → sync → nudge, on repeat, until your target is centered. No two-star alignment walk. Sun, Moon, and planets resolved via live ephemeris.
so-aperion-is-shelved.826e6b: So Aperion is shelved: no longer maintained, never released, and removed from the apps directory. Its goal lives on in the open-source Benro Polaris Firmware Patcher, which is free and does the job better.
that-means-the-loop.dfe0b5: That means the loop closes in seconds even when you're tethered to the mount's air-gapped Wi-Fi hotspot — the only network you actually have at 11pm in a national forest.
that-work-is-open.1d5cd2: That work is open source and free
the-bundled-star-pattern.e4f132: The bundled star-pattern matcher figures out exactly where the camera is pointing — no internet required.
the-closed-loop-that.21a3c0: The closed loop that replaces the two-star alignment walk most mounts still demand.
the-mount-can-now.3d6e4a: The mount can now shoot all night unattended
the-mount-syncs-to.c12065: The mount syncs to the solved coordinate and slews the residual error. Loop until the target is centered.
the-same-astrometry-net.7796aa: The same astrometry.net algorithm that powers every serious astrophotography tool, running 100 % on-device. Bundled star-index files, no internet, no API round-trips — solves finish in under a second on the mount's air-gapped Wi-Fi.
the-watch-you-already.84c866: The Watch You Already Wear, Now in Charge
the-whole-app-as.efffe5: The whole app as it was built: what it did, how auto-align worked, the hardware it ran on, and why it never shipped.
three-tools-one-source.ee4658: Three Tools, One Source of Truth
translation-aligned-integration-with.c89: Translation-aligned integration with on-device star detection. The build-up preview updates every frame so you can watch faint nebulosity emerge in real time.
walk-away-from-the.ae66f4: Walk away from the tripod. The Apple Watch companion gives you the full mount joystick, ISO and shutter wheels, lens picker, framing-corner capture, plate-solve trigger, and a zoomable live preview of both the raw viewfinder and the in-progress stack.
